approachQuestion.prompt:
Ring Sensor Total

Sensors lie on a ring. Array `values` gives their signed readings in clockwise order. Return the greatest sum of exactly k consecutive sensors clockwise, allowing wraparound. Every sensor may be used at most once in a candidate. Return only the sum.

Limits and assumptions:
• 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ k ≤ n; -10^6 ≤ values[i] ≤ 10^6.
• Use the original ring order; sums fit in signed 64-bit integers.

Examples:
1. values = [8,-9,2,7], k = 2 → 15, from the last and first sensors.
2. values = [-3,-2], k = 2 → -5.

Choose one approach.
constraints: Use the original ring order; sums fit in signed 64-bit integers.

options.text: Sum the first k entries. Evaluate each of the n possible starts, replacing the outgoing reading by the incoming reading addressed modulo n.
options.feedback: Exactly n starts represent all ring segments, and k ≤ n prevents a sensor from being reused within a candidate.

options.text: Copy the readings twice into a new array, build prefix sums there, and evaluate the n length-k segments starting in the first copy.
options.feedback: This correctly represents all wrapped segments, but copying and prefix storage can be avoided by modular indexing.

options.text: Check only length-k segments that fit within the array without wrapping.
options.feedback: For [8,-9,2,7] and k=2 this misses the valid sum 15 across the boundary.

options.text: Select the k greatest readings anywhere on the ring.
options.feedback: For [10,-100,9,-100] and k=2 this returns 19 although no adjacent pair contains both positive readings.

feedback.reason: For each circular start, modular indexing identifies the entering reading without duplicating the array.
details: Compute the first length-k sum and initialize best from it. For starts 1 through n-1 subtract values[start-1], add values[(start+k-1) mod n], and update best. Allocate no doubled array.

For each circular start, modular indexing identifies the entering reading without duplicating the array. There are n starts, not n-k+1. Initialize from the first real sum to handle all-negative inputs.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Move around the ring” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Compute the first k-sum and n-1 constant-cost circular updates.
details: The first sum uses k ≤ n additions. There are n-1 constant-work moves and only scalar state. Modular indexing covers all starts, including wraparound, and initialization from a real segment handles all-negative readings.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Each circular shift subtracts and adds one reading; it does not rebuild its length-k sum.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The input is not sorted or doubled; modular indices and scalar sums avoid both the sorting work and copied array.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Only the current sum, best, and indices are retained; no doubled array or prefix table is allocated.
